CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR DECEMBER 12, 2022 AT 3:30 P.M. WILL BE HELD
BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
City
Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of
the public may provide live public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to
the start of public comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item, please
indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker Card Help Line :
If a public comment speaker needs assistance in completing a speaker card,
please call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124. Help line will open
30 minutes prior to the
posted start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the
published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone.
The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the
virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.
Your phone call to the City Council
meeting will be recorded as part of the City Council meeting. By
staying on the line and making public comment during the City Council meeting,
you are agreeing to have your phone call recorded.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting
ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may
submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of the meeting, at the
following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council
prior to the start of the meeting, posted online, and made part of the
legislative record for the item.

LA REUNIÓN ESPECIAL DEL CONSEJO MUNICIPAL DEL 12 DE DICIEMBRE DE 2022 A LAS 3:30
P.M. SE REALIZARÁ POR VIDEOCONFERENCIA/TELECONFERENCIA.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
Para
facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente por
medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la siguiente
manera:
1. Durante la reunión, los miembros del
público pueden hacer comentarios públicos en vivo presentando una tarjeta de
oratoria antes del inicio del comentario sobre el artículo que se está tratando
en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los
oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado en la
agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo
Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el
Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2. Línea
de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pública :
Si un orador de comentario público necesita asistencia para completar su
tarjeta, puede llamar
a la Oficina del
Secretario de la Ciudad al
(626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda abrirá 30
minutos antes del inicio de la reunión.
Después de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pública, únase a la reunión virtual
a la hora de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro dispositivo electrónico
o por
teléfono. Debe usar el
mismo nombre o número de teléfono de la tarjeta de oratoria para la reunión
virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
orador.
Su llamada telefónica a la reunión del Concejo
Municipal se grabará como parte de la
reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al permanecer en la línea y hacer
comentarios públicos durante la
reunión del Concejo Municipal, está aceptando que se grabe su llamada
telefónica.
Computadoras y dispositivos electrónicos pueden sumarse a la reunión en:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Número para ingresar a la reunión por teléfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
reunión: 161 482 446
3. Los miembros del público
pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier longitud antes del inicio de
la reunión a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La
correspondencia se enviará al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de la reunión,
se publicará en línea, y se incorporará al registro legislativo sobre el
artículo.

CITY OF PASADENA

I  City Council Minutes
  December 12, 2022 - 3:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING
  The special meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the organizational meeting to order at 3:40
  p.m. The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Wilson.
  (Absent: Councilmember Hampton)

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton (Arrived at 4: 18 p.m.)
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

I  ADOPTION  OF  A  RESOLUTION
  "CERTIFICATE OF THE CANVASS OF THE ELECTION
  RETURNS" AS PREPARED AND CERTIFIED BY THE LOS
  ACCEPTING  THE

  ANGELES  COUNTY  REGISTRAR-RECORDER/COUNTY
  CLERK FOR THE PASADENA GENERAL MUNICIPAL
  ELECTION CONSOLI DA TED WITH THE NOVEMBER 8, 2022,
  STATEWIDE GENERAL ELECTION
  RECOMMENDATION: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1)  Find that the proposed action is not a project subject to
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) as defined in Section
  21065 and Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines and, as
  such, no environmental document pursuant to CEQA is required
  for the project; and
  (2)  Adopt a resolution accepting the "Certificate of the Canvass
  of the Election Returns" (Exhibit A to the resolution) as prepared
  and certified by the Los Angeles County Registrar-
  Recorder/County Clerk for the Pasadena General Municipal
  Election, consolidated with the Statewide General Election held on
  November 8, 2022 resulting in the passage of Measure L and
  Measure H amending the Pasadena City Charter. (Resolution No.

I
  9970)

  Council Minutes  1  12/12/2022
   · Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, provided a recap of the June 7, 2022

I  Primary Nominating Election results, reporting on the following
  persons as re-elected and elected to Office:

  John J. Kennedy, having received 58.9% of the total votes
  cast for the Office of Member of the City Council from District
  3, was declared to be re-elected to that office.

  Jess Rivas, having received 97 .6% of the total votes cast for
  the office of member of the City Council from District 5, was
  declared to be elected to that office.

  Jason Lyon, having received 51.6% of the total votes cast for
  the office of member of the City Council from District 7, was
  declared to be elected to that office.

  He stated that on July 11, 2022, the City Council adopted
  Resolution No. 9928, accepting the Certified Election Results
  reported by the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County
  Clerk, as stated. As a result of Councilmember Kennedy's sad and
  unfortunate passing on July 21, 2022, the District 3 seat will
  become vacant at the time the City Council adjourns sine die and
  the new term for that seat begins.

I  City Clerk Jomsky reported on the General Municipal Election: On
  November 8, 2022, the City held an election for Measure L (the
  Library Special Tax Measure), and Measure H (the Pasadena
  Charter Amendment Initiative Petition Measure Imposing Rent
  Control).

  Measure L received 40,000 YES votes and 7,280 NO votes,
  with the YES votes receiving 84.6%. To be approved,
  Measure L required a two-thirds majority of the votes cast to
  be in favor and pass, and is therefore deemed approved by
  the voters.

  Measure H received 25,029 yes votes and 21,493 no votes,
  with the yes votes receiving 53.8%.  To be approved,
  Measure H required a 50%+1 majority of the votes cast to be
  in favor and pass, and is therefore deemed approved by the
  voters.

  With 48,852 ballots cast, and 88,291 registered voters in
  Pasadena, the voter turnout for the November 8, 2022 General

I  Election in Pasadena was 55.3%

  Council Minutes  2  12/12/2022
   The following individuals provided comments on the passing of

I  Measure H, spoke on the provisions of the measure, and urged the
  City Council to inform tenants of their rights; and expressed
  appreciation to everyone who advocated for Measure H:

  Jane Panangaden, Pasadena resident
  Ashay Patel, Pasadena resident
  Aeryn Levey, Pasadena resident

  It was moved by Councilmember Williams, seconded by Vice
  Mayor Wilson, to approve the staff recommendation:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jones, Madison, Masuda, Rivas,
  Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Hampton
  ABSTAIN: None

  PRESENTATIONS/  RECOGNIZE OUTGOING COUNCILMEMBERS/STA TEMENTS
  STATEMENTS

  Senator Anthony J. Portantino; Mayor Gordo on behalf of
  Assemblymember Chris Holden; Jens Weiden, Chief Executive

I  Officer of the Rose Bowl; City Manager Miguel Marquez
  representing Executive Management staff; Mayor Gordo
  representing the City Council; all expressed praise and gratitude to
  Vice Mayor Wilson for his many years of dedicated service on the
  City Council, and submitted certificates of recognition and
  appreciation for his contributions to the City and District 7
  residents.

  Margret McAustin, former Councilmember/Pasadena
  resident, spoke in appreciation and recognition of Vice
  Mayor Wilson for his years of service on the City Council.

  Misch Anderson, representing the Pasadena Complete
  Streets Coalition, spoke on the work of Vice Mayor Wilson
  in organizing district walks for Pasadena Complete Streets
  Coalition annual event, participating in walks to school
  days at McKinley Elementary School, his support for the
  creation of the Union Street Protected Bike Lane, his work
  with DOT to get new crosswalks at key streets. In honor of
  these accomplishments, Ms. Anderson, on behalf of the
  Complete Streets Coalition, presented Vice Mayor with the
  first-ever Golden Shoelaces Award.

  Vice Mayor Wilson expressed his thanks and appreciation to

I  Margaret McAustin, Misch Anderson and all the Complete Streets
  advocates and members.

  Council Minutes  3  12/12/2022
   The City Council expressed appreciation and gratitude to Vice

I  Mayor Wilson.

  Vice Mayor Wilson stated that it has been an honor and privilege
  to serve the wonderful residents of Pasadena, thanked the
  professional staff, his Council colleagues, and residents of the City
  for their heartfelt words, certificates and tokens/gifts of
  appreciation.

  Vice Mayor Wilson also acknowl~dged Pam Thyret, District Liaison
  for District 7, for her dedication and expressed his appreciation for
  her many years of service to the community.

  Mayor Gordo recognized Councilmember Justin Jones for his
  service in answering the call to represent District 3 when the City
  tragically lost Councilmember John Kennedy.

  ADJOURN OUTGOING  It was moved by Vice Mayor Wilson, seconded by Councilmember
  COUNCIL - SINE DIE  Jones, to adjourn this City Council sine die:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Jones, Madison, Masuda,
  Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

I  ABSTAIN: None

  City Clerk Jomsky administered
  Councilmembers Rivas and Lyon.
  the  oaths  of office  to

  RECONVENED  Mayor Gordo reconvened the meeting at 5:09 p.m.

  ELECTION OF VICE MAYOR Mayor Gordo recognized the John Muir High School football team
  for their tremendous work at the State Championship game and
  acknowledged all those who supported the team.

  Mayor Gordo provided comments on the District 3 vacancy created
  by the passing of Honorable Councilmember John Kennedy, briefly
  commented on Mr. Kennedy's service and contributions to the City;
  and reminded the community that a special meeting will be held on
  December 15, 2022 to fill the vacancy created by the passing of
  the late Councilmember Kennedy.

  Councilmembers Hampton and Madison echoed the comments of
  Mayor Gordo related to John Muir High School football team
  making it to the State Championship.

I
  The Mayor opened the floor for nominations for a new Vice Mayor.

  Council Minutes  4  12/12/2022
   Councilmember Madison stated that the passing of Mr. Kennedy

I  has brought to light some factors related to the City Charter and
  Municipal Code that that have caused him to consider the role of
  the Vice Mayor. He read City Charter Section 407. - THE VICE
  MAYOR, which states "At its organizational meeting, the City
  Council shall elect from among the Councilmembers a Vice Mayor
  who shall exercise the powers and perform the duties of the Mayor
  during the latter's absence or disability." And Section 2.05.050 -
  Vice Mayor, which states, "The vice mayor, in the absence of the
  mayor or his inability to act, shall exercise the powers and perform
  the duties of the mayor." Councilmember Madison requested that
  the City Clerk look at the role of the Vice Mayor as part of the
  upcoming Charter reform effort. He also spoke on the City
  Council's tradition and history of electing the next senior
  Councilmember that has not yet served as vice mayor, and as far
  as he could tell in the City's history, there has not been a Vice
  Mayor elected to serve with less than four years on the City
  Council. He also noted that with the City's change to coincide with
  statewide election dates, there is now only one organizational
  meeting every two years to elect a Vice Mayor, which is another
  aspect that should be examined as part of Charter reform.
  Councilmember Madison acknowledged that while it may be self-
  serving, he also noted that if one serves for a long time on the City

I  Council, there should be an opportunity to serve as Vice Mayor
  again, pointing out that the current practice is essentially as a de
  facto ban.

  Councilmember Masuda thanked Councilmember Madison and
  Mayor Gordo for providing comments on the City Charter and
  bringing it to his attention that there is no provision in the City
  Charter that requires a Vice Mayor to serve a minimum of one full
  term before being elected in that capacity and stated that he would
  struggle with someone being nominated that has not served at
  least one full term.

  Councilmember Hampton stated that he agrees with the comments
  made; spoke on the passing of their dear friend and colleague Mr.
  Kennedy that brough the details of the City Charter to the forefront,
  stating he is in support of having significant conversation around
  Charter reform, but at this time, feels that the City has a process in
  place to follow, and as such, nominated Councilmember Williams
  to serve as Vice Mayor.

  Mayor Gordo stated that as the discussion surrounding Charter
  reform continues and develops, he feels it would be appropriate for

I  the City to consider some balance in the position of Vice Mayor;
  and stated that he feels tonight there is an opportunity to make the
  residents proud and give them the confidence that their City

  Council Minutes  5  12/12/2022
   Council works together and seeks to do the right thing for the right

I  reasons. He suggested that Council recognize Councilmember
  Williams consistent with the motion as being very qualified,
  consistent with the motion made by Councilmember Hampton, and
  also recognize Councilmember Madison who has served the City
  well and with distinction for decades. He stating that it is his
  understanding that nothing prevents the City Council from
  complying with the Charter by appointing Councilmember Madison
  for the first year and Councilmember Williams for the second year.

  Councilmember William's made a motion to elect Councilmember
  Madison to serve as Vice Mayor from December 2022 to
  December 2023.

  Councilmember Madison requested that the order of the elected
  Vice Mayor be switched to have Councilmember Williams serve
  the first year, noting he preferred serving the second year as Vice
  Mayor, so that it would coincide with the end of his term.

  Councilmember Rivas expressed her support to strike a balance
  and nominate Councilmember Williams and Councilmember
  Madison to each serve one year, while the City looks at the issues
  of the City Charter raised by Councilmember Madison.

I  Following discussion, the City Clerk stated that he intends to bring
  forward a discussion on charter reform at the end of January or
  beginning of February 2023 and suggested the need for task force
  of community members to help vet through all the issues raised.
  He briefly spoke on the timeline and process for the 2024 General
  Election, while stating the information will be spelled out in more
  detail when the item is agendized for further discussion in
  January/February 2023.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Hampton,
  seconded by Councilmember Lyon, to nominate Felicia Williams
  as Vice Mayor, for a term beginning December 12, 2022 and
  expiring on December 11, 2023 and Steve Madison as Vice Mayor,
  for a term beginning December 11, 2023 and expiring December
  9, 2024. There being no further nominations, the Mayor declared
  the nominations closed, and directed the City Clerk to conduct a
  roll call vote, as follows:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Lyon, Madison, Masuda,
  Rivas, Williams, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None

I  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Council Minutes  6  12/12/2022
   The Mayor recognized Felicia Williams as the new Vice Mayor and

I  STATEMENTS/CONCLUDIN
  Councilmember Madison as the Vice Mayor-elect, and introduced
  the newly constituted Pasadena City Council.

  Vice Mayor Williams expressed appreciation and thanks to her
  G REMARKS  colleagues on the City Council for this opportunity and stated she
  looks forward to serving the people in this capacity; and
  acknowledge the opportunity the new Councilmembers will have to
  serve as Vice Mayor.

  Councilmember Madison expressed his appreciation and thanks
  for being elected to serve as Vice Mayor and expressed that the
  City is very fortunate to have such a dedicated City Council and
  looks forward to the bright future ahead; and congratulated
  Councilmembers Rivas and Lyon.

  Mayor Gordo added that this is the most diverse City Council in the
  history of the City of Pasadena, and acknowledged the unique
  perspective and commitment that each member brings to the
  Council. He welcomed Councilmember Lyon and congratulated
  Councilmember Rivas on her re-election, and thanked the City staff
  for all their support and dedication.

  Councilmember Hampton welcomed Councilmember Lyon and
  congratulated Councilmember Rivas on receiving almost 100% of

I  the votes; expressed his excitement to be part of a diverse Council
  and feels it is very promising where the City and the community as
  a whole is heading.

  Vice Mayor Williams stated that she is very happy and proud to be
  here at this moment where the youth in the City can see everything
  on the City Council for the first time in history; stating that the City
  has a great Council that will work well together.

  Councilmember Masuda congratulated Councilmember Rivas and
  Councilmember Lyon.

  ADJOURNMENT  Following discussion, on order of the Mayor, the special meeting of
  the Cit Council adjourned at 5:42 p.m.

  Vic r M. Gordo, Mayor
  City of Pasadena

  Council Minutes  7  12/12/2022
